children: has discovered a software glitch with its 737 MAX series of airplanes that could lead to an automated navigation system to fail during certain landings.
The scenario can occur when pilots change their flight paths due to a missed approach. In one possibility, the crew would have to fly manually as some autopilot features would be disabled.
Airlines operating the 737 MAX were notified of the issue in August, with Boeing adding that it didn't warrant safety concerns, according to a document obtained by

"We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases," Boeing told the newspaper. "Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue."
The company expects a permanent software fix by early 2028.
, two of the largest operators of the 737 MAX, told Boeing that they don't want the new MAX aircraft with the current software, preferring an older version.
The FAA is investigating the matter and will take action as warranted.
